subject: Cloud Computing
title: Machine Learning Data Needs
description: A quick, practical guide to Machine Learning Data Needs.

hook.text: Training a large AI model requires petabytes of data and thousands of GPUs. Only the cloud can provide both at once.

buildup.text: ML needs data storage, processing power, and fast data pipelines — all at scales most companies can't build alone.

discovery.text: Cloud ML platforms — SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure ML — provide everything from data labeling to model deployment.

twist.text: The data is often harder than the model. Collecting, cleaning, and labeling training data consumes 80% of ML effort.

climax.text: Cloud democratized ML. What once required a research lab now runs on managed services accessible to any developer.

punchline.text: AI runs on data. Cloud provides the data infrastructure at scale.

quiz.question: What consumes most of the effort in machine learning projects?
options: Collecting, cleaning, and labeling the training data
Choosing which cloud provider to use
Writing the final model deployment code

details.summary: Machine learning requires large, clean, labeled datasets for training, plus infrastructure for feature engineering, versioning, and serving. Cloud platforms provide managed services for data labeling, feature stores, and training data pipelines that streamline ML workflows.
details.whyItMatters: Data quality and availability are the biggest bottlenecks in ML projects. Understanding ML data requirements prevents the common failure of building models on inadequate or poorly managed data.
takeaways: ML models are only as good as their training data quality
Feature stores manage reusable ML features across teams
Data versioning enables reproducible model training

faq.question: What is a feature store?
faq.answer: A feature store is a centralized repository for storing, sharing, and serving ML features. It ensures that the same feature definitions are used in training and production serving. Feast, Tecton, and SageMaker Feature Store are popular implementations.

faq.question: How much data does machine learning need?
faq.answer: It depends on the task complexity. Simple classification may need thousands of examples, while large language models require billions of tokens. Transfer learning and pre-trained models reduce data requirements significantly for many practical applications.
